text:
noah: Heads-up — customer reported weird rerank scores. Their top candidate has a negative score and none of the scores sum to 1. They think scores should be probabilities. Sample from prod response:
```json
{
  "query": "best hotels SF",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "Hotel A"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "Hotel B"}
  ],
  "scores": [-12.40123, 3.6512]
}
```
noah: Customer says this is breaking their UI because they expect [0..1] probabilities and to show top-3 by prob. Any quick guidance?
maya: Ack. Which rerank endpoint/version are they calling and can you paste the exact request (headers/redacted keys)? Also need customer org id so we can look up logs.
noah: They're on `POST /v1/rerank` using `rw-rerank-alpha`. Request body (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"best hotels SF","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Hotel A"},{"id":"c2","text":"Hotel B"}]}'
```
samir: This is expected/normal: the `score` field from the reranker is an unnormalized model score (logit-like), not a probability. Scores are model-dependent and unbounded (can be negative or positive). If you need probabilities, apply a softmax across the candidate scores: softmax(s_i) = exp(s_i) / sum_j exp(s_j). Use a numerically stable implementation (log-sum-exp).
olivia: I'll add a short note and example to the docs showing softmax conversion and how to interpret top-k. Quick Python example I can paste to the customer:
```py
import math
import numpy as np
scores = np.array([-12.40123, 3.6512])
# stable softmax
shift = scores - np.max(scores)
probs = np.exp(shift) / np.exp(shift).sum()
print(probs.tolist())
```
noah: Customer also reported seeing extremely large values on another call (like 1e+05). Is that plausible?
samir: Very large magnitudes usually come from one of a few issues: model/logit scaling differences across model variants, numeric overflow/underflow in a downstream parser, or the client accidentally aggregating token-level logprobs into a single scalar. Also worth checking if the client parsed numbers as strings and then performed string operations which produced weird results.
noah: Follow-up: I asked them for raw JSON they received. They pasted this and then realized their client was coercing numeric fields into strings and applying locale-based formatting when converting back — causing weird values in the UI. Example they sent (buggy client):
```json
{"query":"best hotels SF","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"Hotel A"},{"id":"c2","text":"Hotel B"}],"scores":["-12.40123","3.6512"]}
```
noah: After fixing parsing to treat `scores` as floats and applying softmax, things matched expectations.
maya: Great. Next steps: 1) reply to customer explaining that rerank returns unnormalized scores (can be negative); include the Python softmax snippet and a JS equivalent; 2) docs update clarifying "scores are model-dependent logits, use softmax to compute probabilities if you need them"; 3) add a Support KB entry (template) for this exact troubleshooting flow (check request shape, check client-side parsing, show softmax examples); 4) note to ML team to include an example in the model onboarding checklist so we call out scale differences per model variant.
olivia: I'll open a small docs PR with examples and copy the KB template into Zendesk draft.
support-bot: ticket #CS-4981 synced — closing internal thread when customer confirms. :thumbsup:
noah: Thanks all — marking as resolved from our side, will reopen if customer sees edge-case after parsing fix. :white_check_mark:
